issues.failure_explanation: The identity is false already for N=2. Using the paper's N=2 table, psi_0=(5+sqrt(15))/6, psi_1=-2/3, psi_2=(5-sqrt(15))/6. Then sum_q a_{0q} psi_q = 7/30 + sqrt(15)/60, which is not w_0=5/18. The proof incorrectly replaces sum_q a_{pq} psi_q by the separate relation sum_q [kappa^{-1}]_{pq} psi_q=1; the matrix a=kappa^{-1}mu introduces the weights w_q.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the false identity or replace it with the actually needed relation sum_q [kappa^{-1}]_{pq} psi_q=1.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma ader_int_prop as stated contains a false relation. The relation is not used in the main derivation of the ADER-DG system, so the main method remains intact, but the lemma is invalid as written.
issues.title: False identity in Lemma ader_int_prop
issues.why_classification: The false identity is isolated and unused downstream; removing it preserves all substantive results.

issues.failure_explanation: For N=1, the first row sum is 1/3 + (sqrt(3)-1)/2, approximately 0.699, but the first abscissa is 1/2 - sqrt(3)/6, approximately 0.211. The simplifying condition C(1) requires row sums to equal abscissas. The correct off-diagonal entries are (1-sqrt(3))/6 and (1+sqrt(3))/6.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the N=1 table by the correct coefficients a_{01}=(1-sqrt(3))/6 and a_{10}=(1+sqrt(3))/6.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed N=1 Butcher table contradicts the method definition and Lemma cn_cond. It does not affect the general theorems, which use the matrix a rather than this table.
issues.title: Incorrect N=1 Butcher table
issues.why_classification: A local computational correction in an illustrative table; no main result depends on it.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof treats q_n as the Lagrange interpolant of the exact solution tilde-u, but q_n is defined by the DG predictor system (eq:snae_lstdg); its nodal values are not shown to equal tilde-u at the nodes. Lemma p_ode_exact only gives exactness for polynomial f(t) with degree <N. A stage-order estimate from C(N) is needed to bound the nodal errors by O(Delta t^{N+1}) before applying the interpolation error bound.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $C(N)$ (\ref{eq:simp_cond}) is satisfied for the IRK-GL-ADER-DG method.
$D(N)$ (\ref{eq:simp_cond}) is satisfied for the IRK-GL-ADER-DG method.

issues.failure_explanation: Butcher's simplifying-condition theorem gives only the lower bound p_RK >= min(2N+2,2N+2,2N+1)=2N+1. It does not imply equality. The classical Gauss-Legendre method also satisfies B(2N+2), C(N), and D(N) (indeed stronger conditions) but has order 2N+2, so the stated implication to p_RK=2N+1 is false. The upper bound p_RK<=2N+1 is not proven here.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add an upper-bound argument ruling out order 2N+2, for example via the Padé stability function or uniqueness of maximal-order methods.
issues.overall_effect: The exact order 2N+1 is not established by the proof of theorem:order_rk. The node superconvergence corollary relying on this exact order is not rigorously supported by this argument.
issues.title: Butcher theorem misused to claim exact order
issues.why_classification: The statement is central; the missing upper bound requires a nontrivial but contained argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The denominator of $R(z)$ is a polynomial $R_{N, N+1}(z)$ of degree $N$.

issues.failure_explanation: For an (N+1) by (N+1) invertible matrix a, det(I-za) has degree N+1, not N. The rank calculation gives rank(a-1w^T)=N, so det(I-z(a-1w^T)) has degree N, not N-1. Thus the degree count does not identify the (N,N+1)-Pade approximant; one must also use R(z)-exp(z)=O(z^{2N+2}) and uniqueness of the Pade approximant.

failure_location.quote: Therefore the numerator of $R(z)$ is a polynomial $P_{N, N+1}(z)$ of degree $N-1$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the degrees to numerator N and denominator N+1, then use the already established order 2N+1 to show R(z)-exp(z)=O(z^{2N+2}) and invoke uniqueness of the (N,N+1)-Pade approximant.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the Pade stability function is invalid as written. The L-stability result and the alternative order proof relying on this Pade theorem are not established by this proof.
issues.title: Incorrect degree count in Pade stability proof
issues.why_classification: The theorem statement is correct and the repair is a local correction plus a standard Pade-uniqueness argument; no main result is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: conditions $C(N+1)$, $D(N+1)$, which are inherent in the classical GL method are not satisfied
Numerical investigation of cases $N = 1, \ldots, 75$ showed that conditions $C(N)$, $D(N)$ are satisfied with precision $10^{-978}$--$10^{-1006}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The corollary relies on C(N+1) being not satisfied, but the paper only reports a numerical check of this fact. The additional remark that p_RK>s does not rule out collocation, since classical Gauss collocation has order 2s>s. A rigorous proof that C(N+1) fails is missing.

failure_location.quote: The IRK-GL-ADER-DG method is not a collocation method according to Theorem 7.7 in~\cite{Hairer_book_1}, since it has the convergence order $p_{\rm RK} > s$ and the simplifying condition $C(N+1)$ is not satisfied.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove rigorously that C(N+1) fails for the ADER-DG matrix, or directly show that a is not the GL collocation matrix.
issues.overall_effect: The non-collocation corollary is not rigorously established by the given argument. The method is indeed non-collocation because its matrix a differs from the classical GL collocation matrix, but the stated proof does not show it.
issues.title: Unproven failure of C(N+1) in non-collocation corollary
issues.why_classification: The statement is true and the repair is a local argument; no main theorem depends on it.
